Reviewing a first-rate production of a second-rate play is hard.
Folded over an unforgettably probing story about family, excellent acting makes Mud Row a theatrical feast.
Mud Row is potent. It shows that an argument about a house is really an argument about who suffered, who escaped, who was left behind and whose version of the family story gets preserved.
This is a solid cast of players making each character feel as real as one can be.
Mud Row does an excellent job of presenting so much without pandering to its audience.
Dominique Morisseau's multigenerational Mud Row consistently falters in delivering an experience worth the weight of its ideas.

cn.t: Morisseau's drama about sisterhood and legacy across two eras earns praise for authentic storytelling, though its structure feels less fresh following another recent Morisseau production. Strong performances elevate the material.
